note: ENV-001's gear=0.08 was not reused: bat mass 0.9kg over 0.85m vs the ENV-001 limb's 0.003kg over 0.58m gives roughly a 600x larger moment of inertia about the hinge, so a much larger gear is required to swing within a comparable fraction of the (much shorter, 0.459s) flight time.

geometry.prep_angle_note: 0.675m from the target point -- far side of the swept range, cocked back
geometry.target_note: front edge of home plate, centered, 1.0m height, matching the fixed B0 pitch
geometry.alignment_angle_note: closest approach of the bat segment to target is 1.3mm at angle=-1.30 rad (fine sweep, step=0.01 rad, range -2.0..2.0)

method: Drive bat_hinge from prep_angle to alignment_angle with sustained ctrl=-1.0, ball moved far away (no ball contact possible), damping=0.05/armature=0.002 kept from <default>, physics_dt=0.0005s, deadline=0.30s (chosen: real bat swings take roughly 0.15-0.2s; 0.30s leaves ~0.16s of the 0.459s total flight time for a scripted controller's trigger latency). Smallest gear meeting the deadline with zero initial contacts and no joint-limit contact is selected.
